    • start

      public void start(String host, int port) throws IOException
      Establishes a connection to a server and initializes the necessary input and output streams for communication. The method also starts a thread that listens for messages from the server.
      Parameters:
      host - the server hostname or IP address to connect to
      port - the port number on the server to connect to
      Throws:
      IOException

    • flushPendingPlayers

      public void flushPendingPlayers()
      If the LobbyController is not yet initialized (e.g., UI not ready), the received player information is temporarily stored in the pendingPlayers list. This allows the application to process and display the player data later, once the lobby UI is available and ready to render the list of players. The block is synchronized to ensure thread safety, as this method might be accessed from different threads (e.g., the network listener thread).

    • sendMessage

      public void sendMessage(String msg)
      Sends a text message through the output stream to the connected server or client. This method attempts to write the message using a PrintWriter instance. If an error occurs during the process, it logs the failure message to the error stream.
      Parameters:
      msg - the text message to be sent

    • sendMessage

      public void sendMessage(MessageDefinitions.Message<?> msg)
      Serializes the provided MessageDefinitions.Message object into a JSON string and sends it through the established connection. This method utilizes the Gson library for serialization and delegates the actual sending to the overloaded sendMessage(String message) method. If serialization fails, an error message is logged to the standard error stream.
      Parameters:
      msg - the MessageDefinitions.Message object to be serialized and sent

    • closeAll

      public void closeAll()
      Releases resources associated with the client connection.

      This method ensures the proper closure of the input stream `reader`, output stream `writer`, and the socket connection. It first checks if each resource is non-null (or in the case of the socket, not already closed), and closes them in sequence. If an error occurs during this process, an error message is logged to the standard error stream.

      This method is typically called to clean up resources when the client disconnects or an issue occurs, ensuring no resource leaks.

    • getID

      public int getID()
      Returns the client ID assigned by the server.

      If the client has not yet received an ID (e.g., before the "Welcome" message), this method returns -1 as a fallback value.

      Returns:
      the integer client ID, or -1 if not yet initialized

    • getMyRobotInfo

      public RobotInfo getMyRobotInfo()
      Returns the RobotInfo record for the current player (bot or human). May return null if not yet initialized (e.g. before start position is chosen).
      Returns:
      RobotInfo for this client, or null if not available.

    • getPendingPlayers

      public List<MessageDefinitions.BodyPlayerAdded> getPendingPlayers()
      Returns a list of players that were received from the server before the LobbyController was fully initialized. This is used by the LobbyController to populate the player list once it becomes available.
      Returns:
      list of pending player entries

    • getMyName

      public String getMyName()
      Returns the username associated with the current client ID.

      If no matching username is found, the string "Unbekannt" is returned.

      Returns:
      the username of the current client or "Unbekannt" if not found

    • getMyFigureFromLobby

      public int getMyFigureFromLobby()
      Retrieves the figure ID associated with the current client from the pending lobby players.

      This method searches through the list of MessageDefinitions.BodyPlayerAdded entries to find the one matching this client's ID and returns its figure.

      Returns:
      the figure ID of the current client, or -1 if not found

    • getUsernames

      public ConcurrentBidirectionalMap<Integer,String> getUsernames()
      Returns a thread-safe bidirectional map of client IDs and usernames.

      This map allows efficient lookup in both directions: from client ID to username and vice versa.

      Returns:
      a ConcurrentBidirectionalMap mapping client IDs to usernames

    • getStartingPoints

      public List<Position> getStartingPoints()
      Returns a list of all starting point positions on the current game map.

      This method scans the locally stored game map and collects all tile positions that contain a field of type "startpoint", regardless of occupation status.

      Returns:
      a list of Position objects representing all starting points on the map

    • setCurrentGameMap

      public void setCurrentGameMap(List<List<List<MessageDefinitions.Field>>> map)
      Sets the current game map.

      The game map is represented as a 3D list structure containing MessageDefinitions.Field objects. It typically models the board layout, where each tile may contain multiple fields.

      Parameters:
      map - the new game map to set
